chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from 'Ali (his brother) from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah and Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband died before consummating the marriage with her, so he said: 'If he had fixed a dowry for her, then she has her full dowry, and she must observe the waiting period, and she is entitled to inheritance, and her waiting period is four months and ten days. And if he had not fixed a dowry for her, then she has no dowry, but she is entitled to inheritance and must observe the waiting period.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The one who died (husband) while she was still his wife
key_terms.لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: He did not enter/consummated with her (before death)

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and dowry rights of a wife if her husband dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *al-mutawaffa 'anha* (death before consummation), establishing that the wife retains full inheritance rights and a three-month waiting period regardless of whether the dowry was specified. The distinction in dowry entitlement—receiving the full amount if fixed, or nothing if merely promised—reflects the Shia juristic view that possession of the body (*dakhul*) is the condition for retaining the dowry, while inheritance is a right of kinship. This ruling underscores the balance between financial obligations and marital status in early Islamic jurisprudence.
